clue.text: This car fitting is switched over with great joy

indicators.note: switched over says the little word is turned round end to end

parts.note: delight is great joy

explanation.surface: A piece of motoring kit that someone is thrilled to turn on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switched over' turns IS into SI, which comes before DELIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A small lamp at the side of a car's front is one of its fittings.

clue.text: I would go over them if contracted the same

parts.note: I'd is the shortened form of I would
'em is the shortened form of them

explanation.surface: A muddled remark about rereading something only if it were shorter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if contracted' tells you to use the shortened forms I'D and 'EM; in a down answer the first sits over the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin word used in references meaning the identical author or work already cited.

clue.text: It provides an outlook from orbit

definitions.text: It provides an outlook from orbit

parts.words: It provides an outlook from orbit
parts.note: orbit suggests space, but it is also the bony socket of the face, from which this organ looks out

explanation.surface: A satellite camera sending pictures down from space.
explanation.definitionFit: The orbit is the skull's socket, and the organ sitting in it gives sight.

clue.text: Comprehensive, fashionable wisdom

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
depth can mean profundity of thought or wisdom

explanation.surface: A list of qualities: thorough, stylish and wise.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorough, detailed study is one that covers a subject fully.

clue.text: Division of race producing excitement

explanation.surface: An athletics qualifying round stirring the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A preliminary round of a race, and also fervour or intensity of feeling.

clue.text: Safety-catch for an estate car?

parts.note: a gun's safety-catch is a brake on firing, while the phrase is also an old name for a type of car

explanation.surface: Asking what safety device a country-house vehicle might carry.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate is a country property where game is shot, and an estate car is a station wagon; the answer is the old name for that kind of car.
explanation.definitionFit: Old British term for a station wagon, originally a vehicle for carrying sporting guns and game.

clue.text: Strengthening check for mortar

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
taken as written
cement is a binding material like mortar

explanation.surface: A builder inspecting the mortar to make sure a wall is strong.
explanation.definitionFit: Support added to make a structure stronger.

clue.text: Cycle retailer and free agent

explanation.surface: A bike shop owner who also works independently.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the answer is a dealer in wheelers, that is bicycles.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone selling bicycles, and a shrewd operator who makes deals for personal gain.

clue.text: Dark solstitial time for Oberon to appear?

definitions.text: Dark solstitial time for Oberon to appear?

parts.words: Dark solstitial time for Oberon to appear?
parts.note: the dark time is night, and Oberon, king of the fairies, appears in Shakespeare's play about a dream on such a night in June

explanation.surface: Asking when the fairy king shows himself on a summer night.
explanation.definitionFit: The June solstice period, whose night gives Shakespeare's 'Dream' its title.

clue.text: Oriental colony in Longton, for example

explanation.surface: An Asian community found in an English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Longton is one of the Stoke-on-Trent pottery towns in England, so it is a china town.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese quarter in a city, and also a town that makes porcelain.

clue.text: Evening accessory?

parts.note: evening suggests night-time dress, but here it means making cloth even, smoothing out creases

explanation.surface: Something to carry with formal wear for a night out.
explanation.definitionFit: A household appliance for pressing clothes smooth.

clue.text: Joyful coppers in country dance

indicators.note: in places the coins inside the dance's name

parts.note: the hay is an old English country dance
coppers are pennies, each abbreviated P

explanation.surface: Police officers enjoying themselves at a barn dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' suggests police, but means pennies, P each, so PP goes inside HAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad and cheerful.

clue.text: Move slowly in order

parts.note: taken as written
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Advancing carefully in a neat line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' looks like a sequence, but is an honour: the Companion of Honour, CH.
explanation.definitionFit: To creep forward a little at a time.

clue.text: Bid made when treasure-chest does not open

indicators.note: does not open means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a coffer is a strong box for valuables

explanation.surface: An offer made at auction when the locked chest stays shut.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal of a price, as at an auction.

clue.text: Plea's changed, bound over, end of Sessions

indicators.note: changed tells you to rearrange the letters of the plea

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A court scene: a defendant alters their plea and is bound over as the sessions close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges PLEA into LEAP; 'end of' takes S from Sessions. 'bound over' reads as a legal term, but only 'bound' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To bound is to jump, so jumps forward.

clue.text: Drinking capacity of king in wicked environment

indicators.note: in with environment says the king sits inside the wicked surroundings

parts.note: sinful means wicked
K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess

explanation.surface: A monarch's heavy drinking in a den of vice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in wicked environment' puts K inside SINFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: As much alcohol as a person can hold.

clue.text: Injunction to gardener to stop work and dance

definitions.text: Injunction to gardener to stop work

explanation.surface: Telling the gardener to put down tools and join the dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: An order to lay a garden tool aside, and also a lively American folk gathering with square dancing.

clue.text: Generator, one 'that draws nothing

parts.note: a magnet is something that attracts or draws iron
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Describing a machine that produces nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A small electrical dynamo using permanent magnets, as in old engine ignitions.

clue.text: Tender too much for a lot

definitions.text: Tender too much for a lot

parts.words: Tender too much for a lot
parts.note: tender here is a verb, to put in an offer, and a lot is an item at auction

explanation.surface: Being far too gentle and loving to many people.
explanation.definitionFit: To offer more than an item is worth at a sale.

clue.text: Young imitator gives story material to jazz-fan

parts.note: copy is the text written for a newspaper story
cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast

explanation.surface: A youngster handing over source material to a jazz lover.
explanation.definitionFit: A child who mimics others.

clue.text: Vulgar song heard from privateer

indicators.note: heard signals that the words are spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a coarse air is a vulgar song

explanation.surface: A rude shanty sung by a pirate.
explanation.walkthrough: COARSE AIR spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mediterranean pirate or a licensed private warship.

clue.text: Gain by Labour

parts.note: the capital L suggests the political party, but it is simply work done for pay

explanation.surface: A political party's election victory.
explanation.definitionFit: To receive money as payment for work done.

clue.text: Gem of small type

explanation.surface: A tiny precious stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A lustrous jewel from an oyster, and an old printers' name for a very small font size.

clue.text: This sea-bird casts feathers tail first

indicators.note: tail first means the last letter is moved to the front

parts.note: to mew is to moult, so a hawk mews its feathers

explanation.surface: A gull moulting backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casts feathers' is MEWS, the falconer's word for moulting; 'tail first' brings its S to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A small duck of northern waters that winters on coasts.

clue.text: Chap running rings round Race of Man

indicators.note: round says the circles surround the race

parts.note: each ring is the letter O
the TT is the motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A man doing laps around the circuit on the Isle of Man.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT (Tourist Trophy) is a motorcycle race on the Isle of Man; two O rings go round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A German man's name, here standing for any fellow.

clue.text: Bad time for Caesar that is classical, almost

indicators.note: almost means the phrase loses its last letter

parts.note: id est is Latin, the classical tongue, for that is

explanation.surface: A gloomy period for the Roman leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Caesar was warned to beware the Ides of March, the day he was killed.
explanation.definitionFit: The mid-month day in the Roman calendar; in March, the date of Julius Caesar's assassination.

clue.text: Take a songbird out-it was fun for kids

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the phrase are put out of order

explanation.surface: Children amused by taking a pet bird outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of TAKE A SONGBIRD.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding a wheeled board is a pastime popular with youngsters.

clue.text: Hairstyle worn by punk bird

explanation.surface: A punk with a dyed mohican.
explanation.definitionFit: A gilded tuft of hair, and Europe's smallest bird with a yellow head stripe.
